document.title: Official Informal for SA Assistant Secretary Robin Raphel and SA/PAB (Islama 01873)
document.publisher: National Security Archive (GWU), The Taliban Biography: The Structure and Leadership of the Taliban 1996-2002
document.note: [Confidential] State notes differences of opinion among high-level Taliban leaders and no well-defined process for communicating decisions. The Taliban are ideologically heterogeneous, including non-ideological Afghans who joined for their own motives. Concedes the Taliban are a fact of life. Previously published in the August 2007 briefing book on Pakistan. Excised.

events.description: US Embassy Islamabad sends cable proposing 'restrained engagement' policy to moderate the Taliban.
Planned Raphel testimony on the Hill.
Raphel remarks at the UN on Afghanistan.
Taliban claim of 'total victory' by next Eid, mid-April.
Embassy Islamabad sends official informal cable recommending Taliban policy options (expel bin Ladin, OIC engagement, UN support, escrow fund).
Raphel's remarks at the UN supporting the UN effort referenced.
US Embassy Islamabad sends official informal cable to Raphel on Taliban policy and 'restrained engagement'.
Raphel's planned testimony on Capitol Hill.
War fought on two fronts, Bamian/Parwan and Badghis, between the Taliban and the forces of Dostam and Massoud.
Raphel's remarks at the UN urging the Taliban to work with Holl for a ceasefire.
Taliban face recent armed opposition in Kunar.

sources_cited: US Embassy Islamabad cable ISLAMABAD 001873 (10 March 1997)
key_claims: The Taliban are not monolithic, with differences among leaders and weak communication of decisions to controlled areas.
The Taliban continue to grant sanctuary to Osama bin Ladin despite US requests.
Harakat-ul-Ansar uses Khost camps, possibly under an ISID-brokered deal with the Taliban.
Pakistan is the Taliban's diplomatic sponsor and tacit materiel supplier, and ISID backs a Taliban victory.
Dostam and Massoud receive supplies from Iran and possibly Russia.
The Embassy recommends 'restrained engagement' to moderate and modernize the Taliban, including pressing for expulsion of bin Ladin.
Taliban are suspected of links with Quetta-based narcotics traffickers.
